title: Artifact inline preview needs the extension in both server MIME list and client TEXT_EXTENSIONS
answers: artifact viewer downloads file instead of previewing it
notebook .ipynb opens as download not inline text
add a new file type to artifact inline preview
artifact served as application/octet-stream but should show as text
body:
Symptom: Opening a previewable text-like artifact (e.g. a .ipynb notebook) in the artifact viewer prompts a download instead of rendering inline text.
Root cause: Two independent lists decide this. Server-side Content-Type comes from mlflow/utils/mime_type_utils.py:get_text_extensions; the client-side inline preview is chosen by TEXT_EXTENSIONS in mlflow/server/js/src/common/utils/FileUtils.ts (ShowArtifactPage.tsx checks TEXT_EXTENSIONS.has(extension), not the served Content-Type). An extension missing from the client set gets no preview even if the server returns text/plain.
Fix pattern: When adding a previewable extension, add it to both get_text_extensions() and TEXT_EXTENSIONS in the same change, plus a parametrized case in tests/utils/test_mime_type_utils.py and a has() assertion in FileUtils.test.ts.
Constraints: Updating only the server list does not enable inline preview; updating only the client set leaves the download Content-Type as octet-stream. Applies to text formats only; binary types must not be added to either list.
applies: Any change to which artifact file extensions are previewable as text in the MLflow artifact viewer.
says: Clicking a notebook in the artifact viewer downloads the file instead of displaying it.
Text files trigger a browser file download rather than opening directly in the previewer.
Enable inline preview inside the artifact tab for newly supported text document formats.
Viewing run artifacts forces a file download instead of rendering text on the page.
Render text artifacts directly within the application viewer without downloading them to disk.
search: Enabling inline text preview for an artifact file extension requires adding it to both mlflow/utils/mime_type_utils.py:get_text_extensions and mlflow/server/js/src/common/utils/FileUtils.ts:TEXT_EXTENSIONS. ShowArtifactPage.tsx checks the client TEXT_EXTENSIONS set while the server sets Content-Type, so updating only one results in download prompts or application/octet-stream headers. Changes require test cases in tests/utils/test_mime_type_utils.py:test_guess_mime_type and FileUtils.test.ts, and apply strictly to text formats without adding binary types.
